rows: I admire your command of the mat. I am afraid tonight you must earn the privilege of putting me on it.
You have a magnificent forearm. A shame they do not award a victory for the loudest sound in the building.
By all means take to the air. Gravity is a very impartial official.
I know a long entrance when I see one. I am not prepared to spend the rest of the evening waiting for you to wrestle.
They may arrange the evening in any order they please. There is only one arrival that makes it an occasion.
Call it the opener if that makes the programme look tidier. I shall treat it as the reason they bought a ticket.
Take a proper look. This is the standard you have been asked to meet.
How touching that you have appointed yourself the attraction. The audience has not yet been consulted.
Do remind me of that distinction once you have taken the first blow.
Of course they deserve a full performance. I wonder whether you have brought one.
Your celebrated {strength}. Yes, I was paying attention. I should hate to deprive you of the opportunity to demonstrate them.
I harbour no personal grievance. I simply have rather different ambitions for the result.
I refuse to conduct an argument at that volume. There is no dignity in it.
A remarkably sensible proposition. We shall see which of us delivers on it.
An elegant diversion. I should like an answer to the original point all the same.
Do not mistake my patience for permission to change the subject.
A fair observation. I shall concede it without conceding the evening.
At last, a point of agreement. Let us not spoil it.
A perfectly proper demand. I regret that I cannot offer you particulars sufficient to sustain the allegation.
I shall not insult this audience by substituting an elegant turn of phrase for evidence. Consider that charge withdrawn.
Very good. We can dispense with the allegation and attend to the actual occasion.
A sensible correction. There is quite enough at stake in this contest without embellishing it with unsupported charges.
The audience may observe which of us can sustain the standard we have promised. I shall submit to that test.
We have a referee to establish the result and spectators to judge the performance. A perfectly adequate arrangement.
I should prefer a demonstration to a recital of unsupported allegations. What can the contest establish?
The audience are perfectly capable of judging a performance. What evidence can we offer them in the ring?
How gratifying that you have devoted such attention to my {strength}. I shall endeavour to make the practical examination rather more demanding.
I congratulate you on your preparations for my {strength}. I would not mistake the rehearsal for the performance, however.
Very well. I shall not dress a supposition in the ceremonial robes of a fact.
A fair objection. Even I cannot award myself the luxury of an unearned verdict.
Your years in the profession are quite admirable. I fear they do not constitute a hereditary right to victory.
I shall gladly acknowledge your experience, provided you do not mistake it for a coronation.
The luxury of experience is knowing when not to accept an apparently generous invitation.
One acquires a certain composure with practice. A novel predicament need not provoke an undignified panic.
How industrious of you to study my performances. I trust you have allowed for a little initiative on my part.
A thorough education, no doubt. I rather suspect the examination will contain a question you haven't revised.
I prefer to study the circumstances in which a technique succeeds, rather than memorise its appearances.
One prepares for several possibilities. It would be terribly presumptuous to expect one's opponent to follow the preferred one.
Ladies and gentlemen, you have paid for an occasion. I shall ensure it consists of wrestling rather than an extended intermission.
I shall spare you a lengthy address. The performance itself is the important part.
A splendid theory. Let us see whether your feet remain beneath you when I attempt the takedown.
You have overlooked one rather important detail: I choose when I leave the canvas.
There is a distinction between wasting time and choosing the pace. I intend to demonstrate it.
I acknowledge your {strength}. The task before me is to overcome them, not admire them.
Enough discussion. The canvas is quite capable of settling this matter.
One fall, if you please, with no assistance from the wings.
If the mat is your preferred stage, I shall be delighted to meet you upon it.
Keep both feet on the canvas for a moment. Let us see how you fare there.
I insist that the performance remain inside the ropes. No excursions into the auditorium.
I anticipate a demanding contest. I will win it.
There is little more to announce. I intend to win.
A clean fall in the centre, with neither interference nor excuses.
I have said all that the occasion requires. The rest belongs to the ring.
I have made my preparations. You may discover their particulars when the bell sounds.
